documents.title: Headaches
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I've been getting headaches a lot since sometime around November, figured it was the job or not sleeping. Lately my heart also does a fluttery thing sometimes when I'm just sitting there. Doesn't last long. Can I come in? Mornings are best, I can be late to the site.

documents.title: RE: Headaches
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for writing. Any chest pain, fainting, weakness on one side, or the worst headache of your life? If so call right away or go to the ED. Otherwise we have Monday 5/9 at 7:45 with the doctor - booked you, reply if that doesn't work.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34M with headaches and palpitations.

HPI: Headaches since roughly last November - dull, both temples or band-like, come on in the afternoon, a few times a week, ibuprofen takes the edge off. No aura, no vision change, no weakness or numbness, not waking him from sleep. Separately, brief fluttering in the chest at rest, seconds at a time, a few times a week. No syncope, no chest pain with exertion. Asked about breathing: admits he gets winded hauling material up stairs on site more than he used to, "like I'm older than I am." No wheeze he's noticed. No fever, no weight change. Caffeine: two large coffees a day.

Meds: OTC ibuprofen prn. NKDA. Smoking 1-1.5 ppd.

Exam: BP 155/95 (rechecked after 5 min, same). HR and SpO2 as charted. Well appearing. Fundi grossly normal, no papilledema. Neck no bruit, thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abdomen: fullness in both flanks - large, smooth, nontender masses palpable bilaterally, ballotable. Soft bruit over the LUQ. No hepatomegaly. Ext no edema, pulses present. Neuro nonfocal.

ECG: sinus, normal.

A/P
1. Bilateral flank masses with elevated BP and a father with polycystic kidneys - this is polycystic kidney disease until proven otherwise. Renal ultrasound ordered. BMP, CBC.
2. BP 155/95 today. Headaches/palpitations could ride along with it. Adding TSH, aldosterone and renin to the draw. Recheck in two weeks with results.
3. Exertional breathlessness in a smoker: albuterol MDI prn for now, see if it helps. Lungs clear today.
4. Smoking - linked it to all three issues today. He listened. Still not ready.

RTC 2 wks.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt per PCP. Creatinine 1.2, upper end of normal. Aldosterone 21, a little above range; renin 3.4. Thyroid and blood count normal. PCP will go over at the 5/23 visit once the ultrasound is done. Ultrasound scheduled 5/17 at the imaging center, pt aware - drink water, full bladder not needed for this one. Pt verbalized understanding.

reports.text: Clinical history: bilateral flank masses. Technique: grayscale and color imaging of both kidneys and bladder. Right kidney measures 15.8 cm in length and left kidney 16.6 cm, both enlarged. Both kidneys contain multiple simple-appearing cysts of varying size throughout the cortex and medulla, replacing much of the normal parenchyma. No hydronephrosis. No shadowing stones. Bladder unremarkable. Liver normal in size and echotexture. Spleen normal in size.
reports.conclusion: Bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple bilateral renal cysts, compatible with polycystic kidney disease in the appropriate clinical setting. No hydronephrosis.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up, two weeks.

Still getting the headaches, maybe a little less. Palpitations a couple of times since last visit, brief. Albuterol: used it 3-4 times on site, thinks it helps some.

BP 155/95 again today, second visit in a row at that level. Exam unchanged - both flanks with large smooth masses, soft LUQ bruit, lungs clear, heart regular.

Data: ultrasound 5/17 - both kidneys enlarged (15.8 and 16.6 cm) and full of cysts, no hydronephrosis, liver normal. Creatinine 1.2. Aldosterone mildly high at 21 with renin 3.4. TSH normal.

A/P
1. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. Father has the same disease with kidney failure. Explained it's inherited, usually progresses slowly, and that BP control and kidney monitoring matter most. He was quiet, said he'd always figured it might be coming. Nephrology referral placed. The mildly high aldosterone fits the cystic kidneys rather than an adrenal problem.
2. BP 155/95 on two occasions. Before labeling hypertension I want home numbers - he'll buy a cuff and log twice daily for 2 weeks and send it in.
3. Headaches / palpitations: no red flags. Watch alongside BP. Less coffee.
4. Ibuprofen: with the kidneys, would rather he use as little as possible. Nephrology will weigh in.
5. Smoking: discussed again.

Portal the log; RTC after nephrology.

documents.title: BP numbers
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Here's two weeks of readings, morning and night. Average works out to 126/80, highest was 138/86 one night after a long day. Headaches have been better the last week or so.

documents.title: RE: BP numbers
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you - that's a good log and those are normal numbers. No medication for now. Keep the cuff and check a few times a week. Your kidney appointment is set for July 20.

documents.title: Nephrology consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEPHROLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/20/2022
Reason: new diagnosis of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease

Thank you for referring this 34-year-old construction worker. Ultrasound in May showed bilaterally enlarged kidneys (15.8 and 16.6 cm) with numerous cysts. His father has ADPKD and is on dialysis. With that family history and the imaging, the diagnosis is secure; genetic testing is not needed for diagnosis.

Creatinine 1.2 in May. He brought a home BP log averaging in the mid-120s over 80. Office BP here 124/80. No gross hematuria, no flank pain episodes, no urinary infections.

Medications: albuterol inhaler as needed; over-the-counter ibuprofen. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: smokes 1-1.5 packs per day, no alcohol.

Exam: palpable kidneys bilaterally, nontender. Lungs clear. No edema.

Impression: ADPKD with preserved kidney function and normal home blood pressure.
Recommendations:
1. No antihypertensive at this time; continue home monitoring, target under 130/80.
2. Please avoid NSAIDs including ibuprofen; acetaminophen is the safer choice for aches.
3. Generous water intake through the day, moderate salt.
4. Kidney function and urine albumin yearly - happy for these to be drawn with you.
5. Strongly encourage stopping smoking.
6. I will see him yearly.

NKDA.
Nephrology

documents.title: Nephrology letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. Agree. Will add UACR to yearly labs.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up.

Headaches have pretty much stopped over the last month; the fluttery heartbeats too. Cut back to one coffee. Home BPs 120s/70s-80s. Saw nephrology - normal BP at home, no medicine, avoid ibuprofen, yearly labs. He admits he still takes ibuprofen "once in a while when my back's wrecked." Went over acetaminophen as the alternative.

Albuterol: uses maybe once a week at work.

BP 128/80 today. Exam: lungs clear, heart regular.

A/P
- ADPKD: per nephrology; UACR with the physical labs.
- Elevated BP readings in May: home log and today normal - resolved, keep monitoring.
- Headaches/palpitations: settled.
- Smoking: 1+ ppd. Not ready.
Physical in October.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 34M.

Interval: ADPKD diagnosed in May, seen by nephrology in July, no meds. Home BPs fine. Headaches gone. Breathing about the same - albuterol a few times a week now, mostly carrying loads up ladders or stairs. No cough change, no wheeze at rest.

Meds: albuterol MDI prn; ibuprofen OTC occasionally (counseled again). NKDA.
Smoking 1-1.5 ppd.

Exam: vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear without wheeze. Abdomen: kidneys palpable both flanks, nontender. Ext no edema. Skin clear.

Plan:
- CMP, CBC, lipids, urine albumin/creatinine for nephrology.
- Vaccines: flu, PCV20 (smoker), bivalent COVID booster - three shots, he was fine with it.
- Breathlessness creeping up: would like breathing tests if this keeps going; he'd rather wait. Reassess at next visit.
- PHQ-2 0.
- Tobacco: same conversation, he knows.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs look stable. Kidney function is about where it was in May, no protein in the urine, cholesterol and blood counts normal. I'll forward these to your kidney doctor.
